is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the required multi-wake visual-inspection skill. I’ll then inspect the current rollout evidence before touching the controller, and keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace.

The visual-first skill requires the evidence to be anchored before image inspection, so I’m pausing policy work while I read the complete workspace/guidance contract, observations, metrics, inherited notes, and the current candidate. After that I’ll compare the keyframes for the best finite sample and the most informative weaker sample.

The sampled set contains no released failure keyframe sheet: all four local solver examples reach the target, and three are duplicate weaker controls. I’ll therefore use the inherited failure metrics only as a negative boundary, while visually comparing the common prewarm, the best finite rollout, and the distinct weaker successful rollout available inside this workspace.

The evidence supports a narrow change: gain 1.7 versus 1.5 is the only policy difference, yet it reaches 1.606 time units sooner, lowers mean distance from 1.919 to 1.874 L, and lowers mean command effort and RMS force/moment. The keyframes show both policies self-propel into the developed wake and approach the target directly, with no collision precursor. I’ll record a one-axis gain-extrapolation hypothesis before editing, as required by the visual-first skill.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The candidate changes only the bounded bearing gain to 1.9; the reusable guidance now ties the parent seed failure, sampled 1.5→1.7 improvement, and inherited instability metrics to a one-axis tuning rule with explicit falsification thresholds.
